requirements.subject: ent:any-value
requirements.canonical: The AnyValue matching symbol `?` matches any value of the specified type.
requirements.original: The matching symbol "?" (AnyValue) matches any value of the specified type.

requirements.subject: ent:any-value
requirements.canonical: AnyValue (`?`) MAY be used for values of all types.
requirements.original: It can be used on values of all types.

requirements.subject: ent:any-value
requirements.canonical: A template field that uses AnyValue (`?`) matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field evaluates to a single element of the specified type.
requirements.original: A template field that uses the any value mechanism matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field evaluates to a single element of the specified type.

ambiguity.issue: 'evaluates to a single element of the specified type' is not defined; it is chosen to mean that the field is present with any value (so an absent optional field does not match).
readings: A template field that uses AnyValue matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field is present and holds any value of its type.
A template field that uses AnyValue matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field holds exactly one value (not a list) of its type.

requirements.subject: ent:any-value-or-none
requirements.canonical: The AnyValueOrNone matching symbol `*` indicates that any valid value and the omission of the given optional field are acceptable.
requirements.original: The matching symbol "*" (AnyValueOrNone) is used to indicate that any valid value and the omission of the given optional field are acceptable.

requirements.subject: ent:any-value-or-none
requirements.canonical: AnyValueOrNone (`*`) MAY be assigned to a template of any type as a whole, to an optional field of a set or record template, or to a value associated with a key of a map template.
requirements.original: It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to a value associated with a key of a map template. a) It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.

requirements.subject: ent:any-value-or-none
requirements.canonical: A record or set template field that uses AnyValueOrNone (`*`) matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field evaluates to any element of the specified type or the field is absent.
requirements.original: A record or set template field that uses this symbol matches the corresponding field if, and only if, either the field evaluates to any element of the specified type, or if the field is absent.

requirements.subject: ent:any-value-or-none
requirements.canonical: A map template key that uses AnyValueOrNone (`*`) instead of an associated value matches the corresponding key if, and only if, the key is present and its associated value evaluates to any value of the specified type, or the key is absent.
requirements.original: A map template key that uses this symbol instead of an associated value matches the corresponding key if, and only if, either the corresponding key is present and its associated value evaluates to any value of the specified type, or if the corresponding key is absent.

requirements.subject: ent:any-value-or-none
requirements.canonical: AnyValueOrNone (`*`) SHALL NOT be assigned to a mandatory field of a record or set template.
requirements.original: a) It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.

requirements.subject: ent:any-value-or-none
requirements.canonical: At the time of matching during a receiving operation, AnyValueOrNone (`*`) SHALL be applied only to optional fields of record and set templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.
requirements.original: b) At the time of matching during a receiving operation, it shall be applied to optional fields of record and set templates or to values associated with keys of map templates only.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether a template that is `*` as a whole (allowed by restriction a) may be used directly in a receiving operation, and whether a violation is a compile-time or a runtime error. The reading that a top-level `*` is not allowed in a receiving operation is chosen.
readings: A template that is AnyValueOrNone as a whole SHALL NOT be used as the top-level template of a receiving operation; `*` is only effective in optional fields and map values.
A template that is AnyValueOrNone as a whole MAY be used in a receiving operation only when it is referenced from an optional field or map value; otherwise the matching causes a runtime error.

requirements.subject: ent:value-range
requirements.canonical: A value range IS a matching mechanism indicating a bounded range of acceptable values, either including or excluding the boundaries.
requirements.original: Ranges indicate a bounded range of acceptable values, including or excluding the boundaries.

requirements.subject: ent:value-range
requirements.canonical: A template field that uses a value range matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field value is equal to one of the values in the range.
requirements.original: A template field that uses a range matches the corresponding field if, and only if, the field value is equal to one of the values in the range.

requirements.subject: ent:range-boundary
requirements.condition: the range is used for values of integer or float types or subtypes
requirements.canonical: When a value range is used for values of integer or float types (or their subtypes), each boundary SHALL be either `infinity`, `-infinity`, or an expression that evaluates to a specific integer or float value.
requirements.original: a) When used for values of integer or float types (and integer or float subtypes), a boundary value shall be either: 1) infinity or -infinity; 2) an expression that evaluates to a specific integer or float value.

requirements.subject: ent:range-boundary
requirements.canonical: The lower boundary of a value range SHALL be placed on the left side of the range and the upper boundary on the right side.
requirements.original: b) The lower boundary shall be put on the left side of the range, the upper boundary at the right side.

requirements.subject: ent:range-boundary
requirements.canonical: The lower boundary of a value range SHALL be less than the upper boundary.
requirements.original: The lower boundary shall be less than the upper boundary.

ambiguity.issue: 'less than' can be read strictly (a range such as (1..1) is an error) or as 'not greater than'; it is also unclear how exclusive boundaries (!) are taken into account. The strict literal reading is chosen.
readings: The lower boundary of a value range SHALL be strictly less than the upper boundary.
The lower boundary of a value range SHALL be less than or equal to the upper boundary.
The value range SHALL contain at least one value after applying exclusive boundaries.

requirements.subject: ent:range-boundary
requirements.condition: the range is used for charstring or universal charstring types
requirements.canonical: When a value range is used in a template or template field of charstring or universal charstring type, each boundary SHALL evaluate to a valid, non-empty character position according to the coded character set table(s) of the type.
requirements.original: c) When used in templates or template fields of charstring or universal charstring types, the boundaries shall evaluate to valid character positions according to the coded character set table(s) of the type (e.g. the given position shall not be empty).

requirements.subject: ent:value-range
requirements.canonical: An empty character position between the lower and the upper boundary of a value range IS NOT a valid value of that range.
requirements.original: d) Empty positions between the lower and the upper boundaries are not considered to be valid values of the specified range.

non_requirement.reason: states that no specific restrictions exist beyond the general static rules of clause 5
